correctness.rationale: With counting input and probability output, character orthogonality produces the unscaled pair-sum energy. When the first pair sum s is nonzero, s³−3s ab determines ab from the cubic sum, hence determines the unordered pair even over nonprime fields. When s=0, evenness puts each antipodal pair into a fiber labeled by 2h(t), and isolated origin separates the diagonal (0,0). The trivial energy is 2S²−∑|f|⁴; the exceptional correction is four times the off-diagonal product sum for each block because there are two ordered representatives per nonzero antipodal pair. On a block of size n with pair masses s_i and total W, equal magnitudes within pairs and aligned products give the bound W²−(3/2)∑s_i²≤(1−3/(2n))W². Strictness within an occupied pair follows from the strictly increasing quadratic in its product magnitude on the nonnegative domain (unless the pair has zero mass); Cauchy–Schwarz forces all pair masses equal at positive W. For M≥2 the maximal coefficient is positive, so the strict sum-of-squares comparison forces precisely one nonzero block, of size M, with no origin mass. For M=1 there are no distinct-pair collisions and the ℓ⁴ term is minimized only by uniform positive magnitude on all q points. Cyclicity gives kernel size 2gcd(m,(q−1)/2) for t↦t^(2m). The numbers on the monomial line are fourth powers as explicitly scoped in the record, not literal operator norms. The supplied verifier was read, not executed. The recorded finite tests cover 81 maps and 648 seeded Gaussian-integer inputs. An independent exact pair-sum check reproduced 5/2 and the perturbed 29/18 in resonant examples over q=7 and q=13, including unequal sizes [3,2,1], and 25/13 for singleton blocks over q=13.
